mainTopic: Objections to carrying knives on the פסח animals on שבת, lessons on haughtiness and anger, and the source that the פסח and תמיד override טומאה.
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא told how the people stuck their knives into the wool and horns of their פסח animals, so the animals carried the knives to the עזרה on שבת. The גמרא now raises objections to this practice. Isn't it using קדשים for work? No, because like הלל they were only מקדיש the animals once they reached the עזרה. But how can anyone be מקדיש on שבת? A קרבן with a fixed time may be consecrated on its day, as רבי יוחנן says. Isn't leading a loaded animal מחמר? It is done כלאחר יד, and whether a מצוה permits breaking a שבות this way was exactly what הלל was asked; he forgot, and he told them to rely on the Jewish people. From הלל's forgetting, the גמרא teaches that haughtiness and anger make a חכם lose wisdom and a נביא lose prophecy, with proofs from הלל, דבורה, משה, אלישע and אליאב. Then the גמרא returns to the קרבנות and asks how we know the תמיד and פסח override טומאה. רבי יוחנן brings a proof from 'איש' in the פסח שני פסוק, ריש לקיש rejects it, and he begins a new proof from the פסוק about sending impure people out of the camp, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't this using a consecrated animal for work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that letting a פסח animal carry a knife is using קדשים for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But surely he is doing work with a consecrated animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the practice it just described, where people stuck knives in their פסח animals so the animals carried them to the עזרה. The problem is that you may not use a consecrated animal for any work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an animal is a קרבן, it belongs to הקדש. Making it carry a load means getting personal benefit from it, which looks like מעילה or a forbidden use of קדשים. So the clever solution for שבת seems to create a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Work, labor (here: making an animal carry something)
Consecrated animals that belong to the Temple
'But surely...', a formula that opens a challenge

phrases.english: But surely he is doing work with consecrated animals!
phrases.notes: The animals carried the knives, which counts as using them for work.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא עָבֵיד עֲבוֹדָה בְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story of הלל's ruling (the knives in the wool), which came on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of having the פסח animals carry the knives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is forbidden to use קדשים for work, and carrying a knife is work.

steps.title: They followed הלל: consecrate only in the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: The animals were still חולין while they carried the knives. They were consecrated only after reaching the עזרה, just as הלל did with his עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They acted like הלל, as a ברייתא teaches: They said about הלל that in all his days no one ever committed מעילה with his עולה. Instead, he would bring it to the עזרה as חולין, consecrate it there, lean his hands on it, and slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the animals were not yet consecrated while they carried the knives. People followed הלל's custom of bringing the animal as חולין and consecrating it only in the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against using קדשים only applies once an animal is consecrated. If you consecrate it only at the last moment, it was ordinary while walking, so carrying the knife was no problem. The ברייתא proves this was a known custom of הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Leans his hands on the animal (סְמִיכָה)

phrases.english: Like Hillel.
As it was taught: They said about Hillel:
In all his days, no person misused his burnt offering.
phrases.notes: Nobody ever accidentally used his consecrated animal.

phrases.english: Rather, he would bring it unconsecrated to the Temple courtyard,
and consecrate it, and lean his hand on it, and slaughter it.
phrases.notes: All of it right away, so it was consecrated for only a moment before the שחיטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּהִלֵּל. דְּתַנְיָא, אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the animals were not yet קדשים while carrying.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the animals were already consecrated on the way.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were חולין on the way and were consecrated only in the עזרה, like הלל.

steps.title: But you may not consecrate on שבת
steps.stepSummary: If they consecrated the פסח in the עזרה, they did so on שבת. A משנה forbids consecrating even on יום טוב, and all the more so on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could he consecrate the פסח on שבת? We learned in a משנה: We may not consecrate, make an ערכין vow, make a חרם, or separate תרומה and מעשרות. If they said all these about יום טוב, then all the more so on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the animal was consecrated in the עזרה, that happened on שבת, and a משנה says consecrating is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fixing the first problem created a second one. The חכמים forbade consecrating on יום טוב because it looks like a business transaction. A קל וחומר extends this to שבת, which is stricter. So consecrating the פסח on שבת seems forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But we learned in a משנה...', introduces a contradicting source
Gifts for the כהן and tithes

steps.confusionAlert: Consecrating is not one of the 39 מלאכות. It is a rabbinic decree, because it resembles doing business. That is why the answer in the next step can make an exception.

phrases.aramaic: פֶּסַח בְּשַׁבָּת הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: How could he consecrate the Paschal offering on Shabbat?
But we learned: We may not consecrate, and we may not make valuation vows,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַחְרִימִין וְאֵין מַגְבִּיהִין תְּרוּמָה וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת.
phrases.english: and we may not dedicate as cherem, and we may not separate terumah and tithes.
All these they said about a Festival,
all the more so on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: פֶּסַח בְּשַׁבָּת הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ, וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Consecrating the פסח in the עזרה on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids consecrating on יום טוב, and by קל וחומר on שבת.

steps.title: Offerings with a fixed time may be consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The ban on consecrating applies only to offerings with no fixed time. A time-bound offering like the פסח may be consecrated on its day, as רבי יוחנן rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only to obligations with no fixed time. But obligations that have a fixed time may be consecrated. As רבי יוחנן said: A person may consecrate his פסח on שבת and his חגיגה on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by limiting the משנה. It forbids consecrating only offerings that can be brought any day, but not offerings like the פסח that must be brought on a specific day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an offering can be brought another day, the חכמים told you to wait. If the Torah requires it on this exact day, the decree does not apply, because otherwise the מצוה would be lost. רבי יוחנן's statement supports this distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This applies only...', limits a rule's scope

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general principle: a rabbinic ban can give way when a time-bound Torah obligation would otherwise be lost.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּחוֹבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן.
phrases.english: This applies only to obligations that have no fixed time.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּחוֹבוֹת שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן — מַקְדִּישִׁין.
phrases.english: But obligations that have a fixed time, we may consecrate.
As Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person may consecrate his Paschal offering on Shabbat
and his festival offering on a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּחוֹבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Consecrating is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Offerings with a fixed time may be consecrated on their day.

steps.title: But he is driving a loaded animal
steps.stepSummary: Leading an animal that carries a knife is מחמר, which is forbidden on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't he driving a loaded animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a third problem with the knife practice. Leading an animal that carries a load on שבת is the forbidden act of מחמר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids having your animal do מלאכה on שבת, and leading a loaded animal is מחמר. Even if the animal was חולין and could be consecrated later, it still carried the knife on שבת while its owner led it.

keyTerms.meaning: Driving or leading a loaded animal on שבת

phrases.english: But isn't he driving a loaded animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא מְחַמֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new objection to the knife practice, separate from the issue of consecrating.
steps.kashyaTarget: Leading the animal with the knife on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leading a loaded animal on שבת is the prohibition of מחמר.

steps.title: It is מחמר done in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: Carrying a knife in the wool or horns is not the normal way to load an animal, so it is מחמר כלאחר יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is driving a loaded animal in an unusual manner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is not normal loading. A sheep with a knife stuck in its wool is an unusual way of carrying, called כלאחר יד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah prohibitions on שבת apply only to the normal way of doing an act. Doing it in an unusual way (כלאחר יד) removes the Torah-level prohibition.

phrases.english: It is driving a laden animal in an unusual manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחַמֵּר כִּלְאַחַר יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Classifies the act as unusual (כלאחר יד).
steps.terutzMaskana: It is מחמר כלאחר יד, which is not a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: Even unusual מחמר is forbidden מדרבנן
steps.stepSummary: Even if כלאחר יד removes the Torah prohibition, a rabbinic prohibition still remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even driving a loaded animal in an unusual manner: granted that there is no Torah prohibition, there is at least a rabbinic prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Doing it כלאחר יד only removes the Torah prohibition, and the rabbinic one is still there. The גמרא is setting up the next answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act done in an unusual way escapes the Torah prohibition, but the חכמים still forbade it. So the knife practice still seems to break an איסור דרבנן on שבת. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted that...', concedes one point to press another

phrases.english: Even driving a laden animal in an unusual manner:
granted that there is no Torah prohibition,
there is at least a rabbinic prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחַמֵּר כִּלְאַחַר יָד נָמֵי נְהִי דְּאִיסּוּרָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the act is מחמר כלאחר יד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כלאחר יד removes only the Torah prohibition, and an איסור דרבנן remains.

steps.title: This was exactly the question put to הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that a rabbinic ban is still in play. It says this was precisely the question the sons of בתירא asked הלל: may a שבות be broken in an unusual way for a מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is exactly what they asked him: if something is permitted by the Torah but a rabbinic ban stands in front of it, may we uproot that ban in an unusual way when a מצוה is involved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge by agreeing with it. Yes, a rabbinic ban remains, and that was the very question asked of הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 7 said that even כלאחר יד leaves a rabbinic ban in place. The גמרא does not deny this. It turns the challenge into the real question of the story: does a מצוה allow breaking a שבות when it is done in an unusual way?

keyTerms.meaning: To uproot it (to set it aside)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting the challenge here. It agrees that a rabbinic ban exists and says that this was the open question.

phrases.english: This is what they asked him:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הֶיתֵּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: A matter that is permitted by the Torah,
and a rabbinic prohibition stands before it,
to uproot it in an unusual manner
phrases.notes: Here, carrying the knife in the wool or horns.

phrases.english: where a מצוה is involved, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּקָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by agreeing with it and saying it was the original question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the difficulty is admitted and identified as the very question posed to הלל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the story meant the action was fully permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbinic ban did exist. Whether a מצוה overrides it when done כלאחר יד was exactly what was being asked.

steps.title: הלל forgot, so he said to rely on the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: הלל says he once heard this הלכה but forgot it. He tells them to watch what the Jewish people will do, because they are the children of prophets.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I heard this הלכה and forgot it. But leave it to the Jewish people. If they are not prophets, they are the children of prophets.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל answers the question from step 8. He cannot remember the ruling, so he says to let the people's own practice show the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving a ruling, הלל points to the people's custom. They then carried the knives in the wool and horns, which shows that a שבות may be set aside כלאחר יד for a מצוה. His forgetting also sets up the next teaching about haughtiness.

keyTerms.meaning: I heard it, and I forgot it
Leave it to the Jewish people

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that the practice of the Jewish people can show what the הלכה is.
steps.whatToRemember: A שבות done כלאחר יד for a מצוה was allowed, as the people's practice showed when הלל could not remember.

phrases.english: He said to them:
This halacha I heard and I have forgotten,
but leave it to the Jewish people,
if they are not prophets —
they are the children of prophets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הֲלָכָה זוֹ שָׁמַעְתִּי וְשָׁכַחְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives הלל's reply to the question in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a שבות be uprooted כלאחר יד for a מצוה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל forgot, and he sent them to learn from the people's practice.

steps.title: A haughty person loses wisdom or prophecy
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: whoever acts haughtily loses his wisdom if he is a חכם, and loses his prophecy if he is a נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: anyone who acts haughtily, if he is a scholar, his wisdom leaves him. If he is a prophet, his prophecy leaves him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a moral lesson that grows out of הלל's forgetting. It states a rule about haughtiness, and the proofs come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to the rule: a חכם loses wisdom, and a נביא loses prophecy. The next two steps bring a proof for each part.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who acts haughtily,

phrases.aramaic: אִם חָכָם הוּא — חׇכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ,
phrases.english: if he is a scholar — his wisdom departs from him,

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָבִיא הוּא — נְבוּאָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: if he is a prophet — his prophecy departs from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמִּתְיַהֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A moral teaching drawn from the הלל story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Haughtiness causes a חכם to lose wisdom and a נביא to lose prophecy.

steps.title: Proof from הלל: he rebuked them, then forgot
steps.stepSummary: The proof that a haughty חכם loses wisdom comes from הלל. He first spoke sharply to the sons of בתירא, and then he forgot the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a scholar's wisdom leaves him we learn from הלל. The Master taught that הלל began to rebuke them with words, and then he said to them: I heard this הלכה and forgot it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first half of רב's rule from the הלל story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the story, הלל scolded the sons of בתירא for not having learned enough. Right after that harsh, haughty moment, he could not remember the הלכה. The גמרא reads the forgetting as a result of the haughtiness.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting a ברייתא)
And then he said to them

phrases.aramaic: אִם חָכָם הוּא חׇכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ —
phrases.english: If he is a scholar, his wisdom departs from him —
from Hillel, for the Master said:
He began to rebuke them with words,
and then he said to them:
This halacha I heard and I have forgotten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם חָכָם הוּא חׇכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ — מֵהִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of step 10.
steps.raayaObject: A haughty חכם loses his wisdom.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about הלל: he rebuked them and then forgot.

steps.title: Proof from דבורה: she praised herself, then needed to be awakened
steps.stepSummary: The proof that a haughty נביא loses prophecy comes from דבורה. She called herself "a mother in Israel," and later she had to be told "awake, awake" to sing.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a prophet's prophecy leaves him we learn from דבורה. It says: "The villages ceased in Israel until I, דבורה, arose, I arose a mother in Israel." And it says: "Awake, awake, דבורה, awake, awake, speak a song."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second half of רב's rule from two פסוקים about דבורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק דבורה praises herself, which is haughtiness. In the second פסוק she must be urged to "wake up" in order to sing. This shows her prophetic spirit had left her.

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָבִיא הוּא נְבוּאָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ —
phrases.english: If he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him —
from Deborah, as it is written:
"The villages ceased in Israel, they ceased
until I, Deborah, arose,
I arose a mother in Israel, etc."
phrases.notes: She's praising herself here, and that's the haughtiness being talked about.

phrases.english: And it is written: "Awake, awake, Deborah,
awake, awake, utter a song, etc."
phrases.notes: She needed to be roused, so her prophecy had left her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נָבִיא הוּא נְבוּאָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ — מִדְּבוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of step 10.

steps.title: An angry person loses wisdom or prophecy
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that anyone who gets angry loses his wisdom if he is a חכם, and loses his prophecy if he is a נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: any person who gets angry, if he is a scholar, his wisdom leaves him. If he is a prophet, his prophecy leaves him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a parallel teaching that uses the same pattern but is about anger instead of haughtiness. The proofs come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure matches רב's teaching exactly. Only the trait changes, from haughtiness (יהירות) to anger (כעס).

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Any person who gets angry,

phrases.aramaic: אִם חָכָם הוּא — חׇכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ,
phrases.english: if he is a scholar — his wisdom departs from him,

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָבִיא הוּא — נְבוּאָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: if he is a prophet — his prophecy departs from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁכּוֹעֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching to step 10, about anger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anger causes a חכם to lose wisdom and a נביא to lose prophecy.

steps.title: Proof from משה: he got angry and the law was hidden from him
steps.stepSummary: משה got angry at the army officers. Afterward, אלעזר הכהן taught the laws of purifying vessels, which shows that משה had forgotten them.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a scholar's wisdom leaves him we learn from משה. It says: "משה was angry with the officers of the army." And it says: "אלעזר הכהן said to the soldiers: this is the law of the תורה that ה׳ commanded משה." This shows the law was hidden from משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first half of ריש לקיש's rule from two פסוקים about משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law was given to משה, so he normally would have taught it. Since אלעזר taught it instead, right after משה got angry, the גמרא concludes that משה had forgotten it because of his anger.

phrases.aramaic: אִם חָכָם הוּא חׇכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ —
phrases.english: If he is a scholar, his wisdom departs from him —
from Moses, as it is written:
"And Moses was angry with the officers of the army, etc."
And it is written: "And Elazar the Kohen said
to the soldiers who came to the battle:
This is the statute of the Torah

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: which ה׳ commanded Moses, etc."
This implies that it was hidden from Moses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם חָכָם הוּא חׇכְמָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ — מִמֹּשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of step 13.

steps.title: Proof from אלישע: he got angry and needed music to prophesy
steps.stepSummary: אלישע spoke angrily to the king of ישראל. Then he needed a musician to play before the hand of ה׳ came upon him, which shows his prophecy had left him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That a prophet's prophecy leaves him we learn from אלישע. It says: "Were it not for my respect for יהושפט מלך יהודה, I would not look at you or see you." And it says: "Now bring me a musician. And when the musician played, the hand of ה׳ came upon him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second half of ריש לקיש's rule from two פסוקים about אלישע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows אלישע's anger at the king. The second shows he needed music to bring the prophecy back, which means his anger had driven it away.

keyTerms.meaning: The hand of ה׳ (the spirit of prophecy)

steps.whatToRemember: Haughtiness (proven from הלל and דבורה) and anger (proven from משה and אלישע) both drive away wisdom and prophecy, even from the greatest people.

phrases.aramaic: אִם נָבִיא הוּא נְבוּאָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ —
phrases.english: If he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him —
from Elisha, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״לוּלֵי פְּנֵי יְהוֹשָׁפָט מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה אֲנִי נוֹשֵׂא
phrases.english: "Were it not that I respect the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַבִּיט אֵלֶיךָ וְאִם אֶרְאֶךָּ וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: I would not look at you nor see you, etc."
And it is written: "But now bring me a musician,
and when the musician played,
the hand of ה׳ came upon him, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נָבִיא הוּא נְבוּאָתוֹ מִסְתַּלֶּקֶת מִמֶּנּוּ — מֵאֱלִישָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of step 13.

steps.title: An angry person loses even greatness promised from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני בר פטיש adds a third teaching about anger: anger can cost a person greatness that Heaven had already set aside for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש said: Whoever gets angry, even if greatness was decreed for him from Heaven, is lowered from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רבי מני בר פטיש, adds one more warning about anger. Anger can cancel greatness that Heaven had already planned for a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said that anger makes a חכם lose wisdom and a נביא lose prophecy. רבי מני בר פטיש goes further. Even a position that Heaven had already decided to give a person can be taken away because of anger.

keyTerms.meaning: they lower him (he loses the position)

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Patish said:
Whoever gets angry,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פּוֹסְקִין עָלָיו גְּדוּלָּה מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
phrases.english: even if greatness was decreed for him from Heaven
— they lower him from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי בַּר פַּטִּישׁ: כׇּל שֶׁכּוֹעֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further consequence of anger after ריש לקיש's teaching and its proofs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anger can cause a person to lose greatness that Heaven had already set aside for him.

steps.title: Proof part one: אליאב got angry at דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source and points to אליאב, who spoke angrily to his younger brother דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From אליאב, as the verse says: 'And אליאב's anger burned against דוד, and he said: Why have you come down? With whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your insolence and the evil of your heart, for you came down to see the battle.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source and begins the proof with אליאב. This part only shows that אליאב got angry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every proof here needs two parts: the person got angry, and the person lost something. This פסוק proves the first part. The פסוק itself says that אליאב's anger burned, and his words to דוד are harsh. The next step will show what he lost.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From Eliav, as it is said:
"And Eliav's anger burned against David
and he said: Why have you come down

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מִי נָטַשְׁתָּ מְעַט הַצֹּאן הָהֵנָּה בַּמִּדְבָּר
phrases.english: and with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness?

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי יָדַעְתִּי אֶת זְדֹנְךָ וְאֵת רוֹעַ לְבָבֶךָ
phrases.english: I know your insolence and the evil of your heart,
for you came down to see the battle."

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן? מֵאֱלִיאָב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the scriptural proof for רבי מני בר פטיש's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That anger makes a person lose greatness from Heaven (first half: showing the anger).
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א יז:כח — אליאב's angry words to דוד.

steps.title: Proof part two: אליאב was rejected even though ה׳ had loved him
steps.stepSummary: ה׳'s special wording about אליאב, 'I have rejected him,' shows that he had once been chosen and then lost it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל went to anoint one of ישי's sons, about all the others it says 'ה׳ did not choose this one.' But about אליאב it says 'ה׳ said to שמואל: Do not look at his appearance or his tall height, for I have rejected him.' This implies that until now ה׳ had loved him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by showing what אליאב lost. ה׳'s wording about him is different from the wording used for his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the other brothers the פסוק says only 'not chosen.' For אליאב it says 'rejected.' You can only reject someone who had been in the running, so until then he had been loved and fit for kingship. Anger plus losing the kingship proves רבי מני בר פטיש's point.

keyTerms.meaning: to anoint them (one of them as king)

steps.confusionAlert: In תנ״ך, the anointing story (פרק טז) comes before אליאב's angry words (פרק יז). Don't get stuck on the order. The point is that this anger was part of his nature, and that is why he lost the kingship that had been meant for him.
steps.whatToRemember: Anger cost אליאב the kingship. He was 'rejected,' not just 'not chosen,' which shows the greatness had really been his before.

phrases.english: And when Shmuel went to anoint one of them,
regarding all of the others it is written:
"ה׳ did not choose this one,"
but regarding Eliav it is written:
"And ה׳ said to Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: אַל תַּבֵּיט אֶל מַרְאֵהוּ וְאֶל גְּבֹהַּ קוֹמָתוֹ
phrases.english: Do not look at his appearance or at his tall height,
for I have rejected him,"

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דַּהֲוָה רָחֵים לֵיהּ עַד הָאִידָּנָא.
phrases.english: which implies that He had loved him until now.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אֲזַל שְׁמוּאֵל לְמִמְשְׁחִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof by showing the loss of greatness that went along with the anger shown in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That anger caused אליאב to lose greatness that Heaven had intended for him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א טז:ז–ח — the contrast between 'not chosen' and 'I have rejected him.'

steps.title: Back to the main topic: how do we know the תמיד and פסח override טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its main sugya. It knows the תמיד and פסח push aside שבת, and now asks for a source that they also push aside טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found that the תמיד and the פסח override שבת. From where do we know that they override impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion about anger is over, and the גמרא goes back to the קרבנות. It asks a new question that sets up the next steps: how do we know these קרבנות are brought even when the community is טמא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא proved that the תמיד and the פסח are brought even on שבת. There is also a known rule that when the whole community is טמא, communal קרבנות are still brought. The גמרא wants the source for that second rule.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a sudden change of subject. The story about אליאב was a side discussion. Now the גמרא is back to the הלכה of the קרבנות.

phrases.english: We have found that the Tamid and the Pesach
override Shabbos;
that they override impurity, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן תָּמִיד וּפֶסַח דְּדָחוּ שַׁבָּת, דְּדָחוּ טוּמְאָה מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the anger discussion and returns to the earlier halachic discussion about the פסח overriding שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the תמיד and the פסח are brought even in a state of communal טומאה.

steps.title: The תמיד learns from the פסח about טומאה
steps.stepSummary: Each קרבן teaches the other: the פסח learned about שבת from the תמיד, and the תמיד learns about טומאה from the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Just as the פסח is learned from the תמיד regarding שבת, so too the תמיד is learned from the פסח regarding impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two קרבנות teach each other. For טומאה, the תמיד learns from the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the פסח learned from the תמיד that it overrides שבת. Here it works the other way: the תמיד learns from the פסח that it overrides טומאה. This only works if the פסח itself has a clear source, and the next step asks for that source.

phrases.english: They say:
Just as the Pesach is learned from the Tamid
regarding Shabbos,
so too the Tamid is learned from the Pesach
regarding impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּיָלֵיף פֶּסַח מִתָּמִיד לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תמיד learns from the פסח that it overrides טומאה, just as the פסח learned from the תמיד that it overrides שבת.

steps.title: How do we know this for the פסח itself?
steps.stepSummary: Since the תמיד's rule depends on the פסח, the גמרא asks for the source that the פסח itself overrides טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסח itself, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question that sets up רבי יוחנן's answer. If the תמיד learns from the פסח, what is the source for the פסח?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 20 shifted the whole question onto the פסח. Now the גמרא needs a direct פסוק showing that the פסח is brought even when the community is טמא.

phrases.english: And the Pesach itself, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפֶסַח גּוּפֵיהּ מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 20 by asking for the source of the rule it relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the קרבן פסח is brought even when the community is טמא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: only an individual is pushed off to פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'איש' in the פסח שני פסוק to mean that only individuals are pushed off. The community brings the פסח on time, even while טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The verse says 'Any man who will be impure from a dead body.' A man (an individual) is pushed off to פסח שני, but the community is not pushed off to פסח שני. Rather, they bring it while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers from the פסוק about פסח שני. It speaks about 'a man,' meaning individuals, so the community is different and brings the פסח in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives a second chance, פסח שני, to an 'איש' who was טמא. רבי יוחנן reads this as limited to individuals. A טמא community does not wait for פסח שני; it brings the פסח on the 14th of ניסן in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: impure from contact with a dead body
the makeup פסח, one month later

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן offers this as the source for the rule that communal טומאה does not stop the פסח, and through it the תמיד. Watch closely: in the next step ריש לקיש rejects this proof, and in step 24 he brings a different source.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For the verse says
"Any man who will be impure from a dead body."
An individual is pushed off to Pesach Sheni,
but the community is not pushed off to Pesach Sheni;
rather, they perform it while impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּאָמַר קְרָא אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶה טָמֵא לָנֶפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'איש' limits פסח שני to individuals, so a טמא community brings the first פסח in טומאה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: maybe the community gets no פסח at all
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש argues that the פסוק could be read the other way: individuals get פסח שני, while a טמא community gets no פסח at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: Say instead that an individual is pushed off to פסח שני, but the community has no fix, neither on the first פסח nor on the second פסח!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן's reading. The word 'איש' could just as well mean the community gets nothing at all, not that it brings the פסח in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the פסוק excludes the community from פסח שני. The argument is over what happens to the community instead. רבי יוחנן says they bring the first פסח in טומאה, while ריש לקיש says the exclusion could mean they lose the פסח completely. So the פסוק alone does not prove רבי יוחנן's point.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, regular פסח on the 14th of ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not stating the final הלכה. He is only showing that רבי יוחנן's פסוק can be read another way, so it is not yet a proof.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Say instead: an individual is pushed off to Pesach Sheni,
but the community has no fix,

phrases.aramaic: לָא בְּפֶסַח רִאשׁוֹן וְלָא בְּפֶסַח שֵׁנִי!
phrases.english: neither on the first Pesach nor on the second Pesach!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference רבי יוחנן drew from the פסוק in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's inference that the community brings the first פסח in טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Excluding the community from פסח שני does not tell us what they do instead. It could mean they lose the פסח completely rather than bringing it in טומאה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש brings his own source: the verse about sending impure people out of the camp
steps.stepSummary: Having rejected רבי יוחנן's proof, ריש לקיש offers a different פסוק as the source that the פסח overrides טומאה. It is the command to send out of the camp every צרוע, every זב, and everyone טמא from a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: the source is from here: 'They shall send out of the camp every leper, every זב, and everyone who is impure from a dead person.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש now gives his own answer to the question of step 21: how do we know the פסח pushes aside טומאה? He quotes a פסוק, but he has not yet explained how it proves anything. The next step sets up that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows that this source replaces רבי יוחנן's proof from 'איש', which ריש לקיש just rejected. The פסוק lists three kinds of impure people who must leave the camp. The proof will come from looking closely at why all three are listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the previous approach and brings a new one.
From here. It introduces a source פסוק.
A person with צרעת (a spiritual skin disease)
A man with an impure bodily discharge
Someone impure from contact with a dead body (טמא מת)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ריש לקיש is talking about the קרבן פסח directly here. His פסוק is about who must leave the camp. He will use it to show that טומאת מת is treated differently in some situation, and that situation will turn out to be the פסח.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: from here:
phrases.notes: He replaces רבי יוחנן's source, which he just challenged.

phrases.english: "They shall send out of the camp
every leper and every zav
and everyone impure from a dead person."
phrases.notes: This person is a טמא מת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבי יוחנן's reading in step 23, ריש לקיש offers his own source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the קרבן פסח pushes aside טומאה (from step 21).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק 'וישלחו מן המחנה כל צרוע וכל זב וכל טמא לנפש'. The explanation follows in the next steps.

steps.title: Why does the verse need to mention זבין and מצורעין at all?
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש points out that the פסוק seems to have extra words. If even a טמא מת, whose impurity is lighter, is sent out, then זבין and מצורעין, who are more severe, should obviously be sent out by קל וחומר. So why does the פסוק list them?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק mention only those impure from a dead body and not mention זבין and מצורעין. I would figure it out myself: if those impure from a dead body are sent out, then זבין and מצורעין should surely be sent out too!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש is raising a question on the wording of his own פסוק. He is setting up a דרשה: since the extra words seem unnecessary, they must be teaching something new, and that answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא מת got his impurity from outside, from a dead body. A זב and a מצורע are the source of their own impurity, so they are more severe. By קל וחומר, if the lighter case is sent out, the stricter cases surely are. Naming them looks extra, and the גמרא will use this to show there is a case where the stricter ones are sent out but the טמא מת is not, which is the פסח brought in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it say this and not say that. A formula pointing out extra words in a פסוק.
People impure from a dead body
They are sent out (of the camp)
All the more so. This signals a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not really questioning whether זבין and מצורעין are sent out. They certainly are. He is pointing out that the פסוק spelled out something we could have figured out ourselves, which means those words must have another purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'extra words' pattern is a classic way the גמרא builds a דרשה. A קל וחומר shows that a phrase is not needed for its plain meaning, so the phrase is used to teach something new.

phrases.english: Let it say those impure from the dead
and not say zavin and lepers,
and I would say on my own:
phrases.notes: Meaning: I could learn it myself through logic.

phrases.english: if those impure from the dead are sent out,
phrases.notes: Their impurity comes from outside, so it is lighter.

phrases.english: zavin and lepers, all the more so, no?
phrases.notes: Their impurity comes from their own bodies, so it is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵאָמֵר טְמֵאֵי מֵתִים וְאַל יֵאָמֵר זָבִין וּמְצוֹרָעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins explaining how the פסוק quoted in step 24 works as a proof, by showing that part of it seems unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the פסוק 'וישלחו מן המחנה', specifically its mention of זב and צרוע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the lighter טמא מת to the stricter זב and מצורע makes naming them seem unnecessary. This sets up a דרשה from the extra words.
